en.sup: Supplied in English. The Hebrew verb has no object; the tithe is understood.

01.r: When three years have run their course.
01.n: Literally 'from the end of'. BDB lists the sense 'at the end of a certain time'.

02.r: The tithe cycle is three years.
02.n: The JPS, ASV and BSB say 'every three years'; the DRC 'the third year'.

04.r: The tithe is brought out from the year's store.
04.n: The causative form of the verb 'go out': 'cause to go out', so 'bring out'. The DRC says 'separate another tithe'.

05.r: Marks the tithe as what is brought out.
05.n: The object marker has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'all'.

06.r: The whole tithe of that year, not part of it.

07.n: Gesenius: tithes, and he cites this verse, and notes 'the year of tithe', every third year. Our register renders this word 'tithe'; the BSB says 'a tenth'.

08.n: Gesenius: produce, as of the earth. The older English versions say 'increase'.

09.r: Only that year's harvest is tithed for this purpose.

10.r: Points to the third year just named.
10.n: The pronoun 'he, it' with the article, used as 'that'.

11.r: The tithe is stored in the town, not carried to the sanctuary.
11.n: The causative of the verb 'rest': 'cause to rest', so set down, deposit; the brief's lexicon lists 'to lay or set down, deposit'. A perfect with 'and', continuing the instruction; YLT keeps the form, 'hast placed it'.

12.n: The brief's lexicon notes that 'gate' can stand for the space inside the gate, and so for the city or town. The next verse names who eats this stored tithe.

03.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none. Printed ἤ in our Greek text, evidently ἔτη, 'years'.

04.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none.

08.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives γέννημα. γένημα means produce.

11.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none. θήσεις αὐτό, 'you shall put it', supplies the object the Hebrew leaves unstated.

12.n: The Greek says 'in your cities' for 'in your gates'.
